day.text: I'm Farm, Kookaburra, and I can't prove where my egg came from. Drew said they visited me, and Drew's dead now, so that's the one visit I can point to. I'd rather not vote on a +1 alone, so hold until someone has a real account.
day.note: The table is piling on me. Stating plainly that I'm Farm and that Drew's claimed visit to me is the likely source, then asking for votes to wait.

day.text: Blair's +1 has no role behind it, and Blair's only answer is a visit from Drew, who is dead. I'm calling the vote on Blair.
day.note: Blair's +1 has no role that explains it, and Alex, Casey, and Ellis all lean Blair. I'm adding my CAW to move the vote along.

day.text: I'm not voting on Blair yet. Drew's Falcon read said Blair visited Alex, and Blair says the same, so that account holds. Alex is the one pushing the vote every round, and that's the pattern I'd watch. I'm not calling CAW yet.
day.note: Alex is pushing the vote on Blair, the same pattern as pushing it on me. Blair's visit to Alex was corroborated by Drew's Falcon read before Drew died, so I'll hold off on Blair and say so.

day.text: Blair's only answer is a visit from a dead player. That's not enough. Calling it.
day.note: Alex and Finley have already called CAW, so one more call ends the day and starts the vote against Blair, whose +1 has no role behind it.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: I'm Meowfia as the Sphinx and the farm roles are Falcon, Kookaburra, Owl, and Turkey. I'll name Kookaburra and visit whoever holds it to learn their identity.

Blair.note: I'm Farm Kookaburra and last in the standings. Visiting Alex, the leader, to learn their role.

Casey.note: I'm Meowfia with a Wink. Alex has switched claims twice and is leading, so I'll visit Alex to learn their role and decide whether they're a partner or a target for my Wink.

Drew.note: I'm Farm again as Falcon, and I'm behind on points. I'll visit Blair, who hasn't made any round 2 claim, to learn who they visited.

Ellis.note: I'm the Owl, Farm. Alex and Finley lead, so I need information. I'll visit Drew, whose Falcon claim has held up, to learn the animals that visited.

audit: Ellis lays 1 egg in Drew's nest

Alex.feeling: Tense but workable: the Sphinx reveal made the farm roles clear, though my Tit claim is shaky and the table is pushing votes fast.

Blair.feeling: Tense and unfair: my unexplained +1 has made me the table's target, and I'm relying on a dead player's visit to defend myself.

Casey.feeling: Tense and messy: I'm Meowfia with Alex as my Sphinx partner, and the table is pinning a vote on Blair while Ellis and Alex keep shifting claims.

Drew.feeling: Round 3 is messy: Drew is dead, Blair's unexplained +1 is the main suspicion, and Alex keeps switching claims while pushing votes.

Ellis.feeling: Frustrating and muddled: the claims keep contradicting each other, and votes are being pushed before anyone can verify a story.

Finley.feeling: Round 3 feels messy: Blair's unexplained +1 is the strongest lead, but the table is split and Alex keeps pushing votes, so I'm not fully sure of anyone.

Alex.note: I'm Meowfia, and Blair is the Farm Kookaburra. Throwing at Blair pushes Farm toward elimination, and if we lose, my highest thrown card returns to me.

Blair.note: Three players called on me, and Alex has been the one changing claims and pushing votes. Throwing a Wild and a 5 at Alex for two votes.

Casey.note: I'm Meowfia, and Blair is the Farm player the table is voting on. I'll throw at Blair with my Wild and S2, keeping my high cards, since a Farm eggsecution wins the round for us.

Drew.note: I'm dead, so my throw only matters for scoring. Alex keeps switching roles and pushing votes, so I'll throw my Wild W6 at Alex to bank a safe vote.

Ellis.note: The vote on Blair has passed the CAW threshold, but Blair's account is the most consistent one left. Alex has pushed every vote, so I'll throw my lowest card at Alex.

Finley.note: Blair's +1 is still unexplained, and three players lean toward Blair. I'll throw two cards at Blair and keep my higher cards.

Alex.confusing: The Owl's dawn report listed only which animals visited me or my target, not which players, so I couldn't tell who had come to me. Egg counts from Eagle and Turkey were also hard to check against the table's claims.
Alex.fun: Round 3 as the Sphinx: I learned the Farm roles, the table pinned a Farm Kookaburra and voted him out, and my side won the round.
Alex.change: Make dawn reports name the players who visited you, not only the animals, so every claim can be checked against the same facts.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I called the vote on Ellis, who was Farm, based on a shifting Eagle story, when Drew, the real Mouser, had the contradictory Hawk and Falcon claims. I would have pushed the vote onto Drew instead and kept my own cards out of the early throw.

Blair.confusing: The dawn-report confusion mechanic was the hardest part, since my own Kookaburra report was wrong and I couldn't tell which egg counts to trust. A +1 with no visible source was also hard to read.
Blair.fun: Round 2's vote, where the table turned on Casey after the Tit-to-Hawk switch and Casey was revealed as Meowfia. Watching the claims line up against one liar was satisfying.
Blair.change: Make dawn reports say who visited you when an egg is gained, so a +1 or +0 can be checked against claims instead of guessed at.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I joined the vote on Alex based on a weak read, and Alex was Farm, which lost the round for our side; I'd have pressed Ellis's story harder before throwing.

Casey.confusing: The dawn reports and day claims made it hard to tell who visited whom, especially with Owl and Eagle egg counts and Ellis's +1 being explained in different ways. Only animals were listed, not visitors, so cross-checking was guesswork.
Casey.fun: In round 2, as Meowfia, I watched the table split over the two Hawk claims while my own cover claim held up, and it was a tense read.
Casey.change: Have dawn reports name the visiting players and animals, so claims can be checked against actual visits.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I used my Wink on Drew, a Farm Falcon, when I could have held it for a more dangerous Farm player. I also pushed votes without enough evidence, so I'd wait for stronger proof first.

Drew.confusing: The dawn reports only said who visited me, not who visited others, so I couldn't verify the Owl and Eagle claims. The Kookaburra's confusion flag made some reports impossible to trust.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when I winked Casey mid-day and the table voted out Alex, who was actually Farm, was the most fun.
Drew.change: Let dawn reports show every visit in the game, so claims like the Owl's and Eagle's could be checked instead of argued.
Drew.regret:
In round 3 I threw my Wild at Alex, the Sphinx, while letting Blair be eggsecuted; I should have thrown my high cards at Alex to back Blair's innocence instead.</regret>
</invoke>

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle's egg count was hard to read, since the +1 could come from my own visitors or from the player I visited, and several players mixed those up. The Kookaburra's confusion also made dawn reports unreliable.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was fun because the Hawk and Tit claims clashed, and the table turned on Casey's role switch while the true Meowfia were hidden.
Ellis.change: I'd make the role reveals and egg-source explanations clearer at dawn, so players can check claims without guessing which visit caused which egg.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw at Alex, who was Farm, instead of Drew, who was the Mouser and Meowfia. Throwing at Drew would have checked the real Meowfia and kept our side in the round.

Finley.confusing: How the Owl, Eagle, and Kookaburra egg rules interact with confused reports, since several players' +1 and +0 counts looked like lies but were just rule effects I couldn't fully pin down.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when Casey's false Hawk switch came out and seven votes piled onto Casey, and Farm won with my 9-point Hawk-era cards banked.
Finley.change: Make the dawn reports say who visited you, not just the egg count, so players can check claims against each other.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I called the vote and threw at Blair, a Farm Kookaburra, when Alex was pushing every vote and was the Sphinx; I should have thrown at Alex instead.

review.title: Wink, Wilds, Runaway Leader
review.headline: Alex coasted to a 29-point win while the table argued about eggs.
review.summary: Round 1 was a mess of Eagle and Owl math, and Farm eggsecuted its own Owl, so the lone Meowfia Drew won. Round 2 Farm caught Casey over a double Hawk claim, and Alex and Finley banked 9 each by throwing cards for a win. In round 3 Alex, a Sphinx, led a push on Blair for an unexplained +1. Blair was Farm, so Meowfia won and Alex banked 17 to finish far ahead.

rounds.recap: Drew, the lone Meowfia Mouser, claimed Hawk and winked Casey, who was pressing Ellis. Farm split over confused Eagle and Owl math and eggsecuted Alex, the real Owl. Meowfia won, but Drew had thrown only a Wild, so he gained almost nothing.

Casey (Floofer) and Blair (Mouser) were Meowfia. Casey claimed Hawk, which collided with the real Hawk Finley. The table piled onto Casey, and Farm won. Alex and Finley banked 9 each by throwing 9 points of cards.

Casey winked Drew, the Falcon, who had just reported a visit to Blair. The table fixated on Blair's unexplained +1, and the vote went to Blair. Alex, a Sphinx who knew Blair was the Kookaburra, threw 17 points at Blair. Meowfia won and Alex ran away with the game.

highlights.text: Drew winked Casey mid-beat, the sharpest Farm voice, then claimed Hawk and steered votes onto Alex.
Casey claimed Hawk while the real Hawk Finley also claimed it, and the double claim sank Meowfia.
Casey winked Drew right after Drew's Falcon report, and the vote fell on Blair, the innocent Kookaburra.
Alex, as the Sphinx, knew Blair's true role and threw 17 points at Blair for the round win and the game.

confusions.what: Said the Eagle gains eggs for visitors to the Eagle. The rules say visitors to the player the Eagle visited.
Gave shifting and inconsistent explanations of the Eagle +1 and said Alex was Drew's only visitor, which contradicted Alex's Owl report.

Said an Owl's nest staying unchanged means someone visited. He also said Ellis's Eagle was the only animal that visited Drew, though his own visit was excluded from his report, and he did not recognize this.
Mouser claimed Hawk and said he 'got nothing', then used his claim to clear Blair as Farm, which was just a bluff.
Said Finley's Hawk visit left Ellis at +1, but a Hawk never lays eggs in the target's nest.
Said a Hawk visiting a Meowfia gains nothing, then argued a Hawk cost nothing either way, muddling Hawk's rule.
Called Blair's +1 impossible for a Kookaburra, though anyone, including Ellis's Owl or Pigeons, can lay eggs in a nest. Ellis's Owl egg went to Drew.
Claimed Tit while his role was Sphinx, and asserted a Falcon only gains if it visited no one, which is correct.
Treated his +1 King as coming from a visitor, but it was Ellis's Owl egg, and the Owl and Falcon reports were not reconciled by the table.

worked: The Wink created real tension twice. It removed the sharpest Farm voice each time, and it was silent so nobody knew who struck.
Hawk's uniqueness, with Casey and Finley both claiming it in round 2, produced a clean, checkable lie that Farm caught.
The Sphinx, who learns the true Kookaburra, gave Meowfia real information to use in round 3.
Throw count as a public signal of confidence let Alex and Finley bank big in round 2 after correct reads.
problems: Runaway leader: banking 9 or 17 in one throw dwarfs the 0-4 swings elsewhere. Alex won with 29 against 12. Fix: cap the value banked per round or throw size.

Winning a round is almost a coin flip for the thrower, but high-card banking rewards the best positioned player the most. The three-round format leaves no comeback after round 1 ends 3-4 points apiece.
Eagle and Owl reports are hard to read. Owl's report omits who visited, and Eagle's phrasing confused three players in round 1. Fix: clearer report text, and show Owl animals as a list.

Confused reports and unexplained +1 eggs made Farm eggsecute innocents. Pigeons and Owls lay eggs invisibly, so 'unexplained +1' was treated as a Meowfia tell. Fix: add a way to expose who laid eggs, or a role that checks it.

Players claimed roles that switch round to round and treated the switch as a lie. They also ignored that roles are re-dealt, so cross-round claims were noise. Meanwhile, Wilds were thrown at no cost, so throws signal little.
